title: Defining the adipose immune environment in PDAC associated cachexia and pre-cachexia weight loss
summary: Pancreatic cancer is a very aggressive disease with still very poor survival rates. Many patients diagnosed with pancreatic cancer suffer from cachexia during the course of the disease. Cachexia leads to severe weight loss with a reduction in both fat mass and muscle mass, which is associated with a significant decline in quality of life. From other metabolic disorders, such as obesity, it is known that changes in adipose tissue play a central role in disease development and maintenance. The role of changes in adipose tissue in pancreatic cancer-associated cachexia has not been sufficiently studied to date. Therefore, the aim of this study is to comprehensively characterize and understand the changes in adipose tissue in pancreatic cancer-associated cachexia.

interventions.name: Control group: Living kidney donors - intraabdominal and subcutaneous adipose tissue was collected intraoperatively
Pancreatic cancer patients without cachexia (defined by body weight development over the last six months) - intraabdominal and subcutaneous adipose tissue was collected intraoperatively
Pancreatic cancer patients with cachexia (defined by body weight development over the last six months) - intraabdominal and subcutaneous adipose tissue was collected intraoperatively

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Suspected pancreatic cancer (for pancreatic cancer groups)
- healthy kidney donors (control group)
- Written informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
- Chronic inflammatory diseases
- History of cancer diagnosis
